name: message-thread
purpose: The conversation of a support ticket, oldest first, as Help Scout, Front, Plain and the Zendesk Agent Workspace show it: each message names its author (avatar, name, customer or agent), the channel it came by, when it was sent and, for email, who received it; then the body, the attachments and the quoted previous messages behind a toggle. Three types of item share the list: a public reply, an internal note (a warning band labelled "Internal note", so it never reads as a reply sent to the customer), and a system event line ("Jane Doe changed status to Pending"). A long middle collapses behind "Show 6 earlier messages". It is not `ChatMessage`, which is the generative AI chat (decision SUP-03).
useWhen: The conversation on a support ticket or a customer case: the customer's emails and chats, the agents' replies, the internal notes agents leave each other, and the status changes in between.
An email-style message history where each message shows its sender, recipients (To, Cc), channel, attachments and the quoted text of earlier messages.
A ticket that mixes public replies and private notes, where an agent must see at a glance which messages the customer can read.
avoidWhen: A chat with the generative AI assistant → `chat-message` inside `conversation`.
A log of what happened to a resource, with no messages (deploys, status changes, audit entries) → the Timeline component planned in SUP-01.
A single notice on a page → `alert`.
Comments on a code line or a review → not this component; it carries support semantics (channels, recipients, internal notes).
related: `chat-message` — the AI conversation turn (`from: user | assistant | system`, feedback thumbs, regenerate). A ticket has customers and agents, notes, channels and recipients instead (SUP-03).
Timeline (planned in SUP-01) — an activity log of events; a thread interleaves a few event lines between messages.
`timestamp` — the sent time of each item; it opens the full date in every zone.
`file-token-group`, `file-preview` — the attachments composed into an item's `attachments` slot.
`icon-button`, `dropdown-menu` — the Reply button and the More menu (Forward, …) composed into an item's `actions` slot.
bestPractices: Render the items oldest first; the newest message sits at the end, next to the reply composer.
Put every message after the first two and before the last three in a `MessageThread.Group` once a thread holds more than eight, so the newest messages stay in view.
Pass `count` on the Group with the number of items it holds; the button reads it.
Use `type="note"` for anything only agents can read; never colour a reply to make it look private.
Put the text of earlier messages that an email quotes in the `quoted` slot, not in the body, so the reader sees only what is new.
Keep the `actions` slot short: Reply as an `IconButton`, Forward and the rest as items of a More `DropdownMenu`.
Write an event line as one short sentence that names who did what ("Jane Doe changed status to Pending").

props.name: timestampFormat
props.doc: How every item's sent time reads: `relative` (`2 hours ago`), `local` date and time, `utc`, or `time` (hour and minute only) — Timestamp's own union.

props.name: loading
props.doc: Shows three placeholder messages in place of the items while the thread loads, and marks it busy.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.doc: Accessible name of the list. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Conversation`).

slots.name: default
slots.notes: The `MessageThread.Item` and `MessageThread.Group` children, oldest first. Not rendered while `loading`.
